blocks.text: If u is differentiable and homogeneous of degree n, \(xu_x+yu_y=nu\). With continuous second partials, \(x^2u_{xx}+2xyu_{xy}+y^2u_{yy}=n(n-1)u\).
If \(u=\log f\) and f is homogeneous of degree n, then \(xu_x+yu_y=n\); in particular it is 1 when n=1.

items.title: Euler: square root
paragraphs: For positive k, \(u(kx,ky)=ku(x,y)\); the degree is one. Away from the origin, \(u_x=x/u,u_y=y/u\).

items.title: Euler: rational function
paragraphs: The quotient is homogeneous of degree one where x+y≠0. Quotient differentiation gives \(u_x=y^2/(x+y)^2\), \(u_y=x^2/(x+y)^2\).

items.title: Logarithm of a homogeneous function
paragraphs: Put v=(x²+y²)/(x+y), homogeneous of degree one on the logarithm’s real domain. Euler gives \(xv_x+yv_y=v\).
Because \(u_x=v_x/v,u_y=v_y/v\), their weighted sum is v/v=1.

textbook_match.note: Example 5.11 takes log u to be a degree-two quotient. Here u itself is the logarithm of a degree-one quotient.
